earlier_scan.source_named: Foley, Sean. 2020. Naruo: an endangered Ngwi language spoken in Yunnan, China. Paper at ICSTLL-53, Univ. of North Texas. 7pp.
earlier_scan.note: Foley 2020 conference paper (only sketch of the language) not online; other refs are tone/survey works in Chinese

sources.citation: Yang, Cathryn; Kwok Wailing 范秀琳; Zhou Decai 周德才; Yang Wenjing 杨文静. 2017. 滇西北彝语他留土语群：忠诚的南诏战士 / The Taloid cluster of Northwestern Yunnan: Loyal Soldiers of the Nanzhao Kingdom. Presented at ICSTLL 50, Beijing. 8 pp. (slides, Chinese). Read as the academia.edu page text captured by the the Internet Archive (2025-05-15); the PDF itself is login-gated.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Historical-dialectology slides: lists 纳若 (水田) as Taloid member no. 5 (data from 2013 fieldwork), gives shared Taloid innovations (*a > u, *ak > a̱, *(-)rwe > ua), tone reflexes and lexical innovations; no mention of stress/重音/韵律.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) Languages. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Naluo mentioned only when reviewing Bradley 2007's inventory (pp. 52-53); Lavu (Yongsheng) is used to represent the Talu/Shuitian/Zhili/Luo/Ziyi group; no Naluo profile and nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record nalu1239 and English Wikipedia 'Naruo language' (citing Bradley 2004 ICSTLL-37 keynote; You Weiqiong 2013; Yongsheng Xianzhi 1989; Yunnan Minzu Shibie Yanjiuzu 1954 wordlist report).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Orientation only (classification, demography, subgroup names); nothing on stress. Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description 'Wang Chengyou 2003' covers Yongsheng Yi = Talu, not Naruo.

sources.citation: Foley, Sean. 2020. Naruo: an endangered Ngwi language spoken in Yunnan, China. Paper presented at ICSTLL-53, University of North Texas, October 2020. 7 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only first-hand linguistic description devoted to Naruo (Glottolog 710773); if any statement on syllable prominence/stress exists for this language it would be here. Hammarström holds a copy (hh bibliography); ask the author (SIL East Asia) or H. Hammarström.

sources.citation: 周德才 Zhou Decai. 2004. 他留话研究 [A study of Taliu]. Kunming: Yunnan Minzu Chubanshe. 297 pp; and 胡素华, 段秋红 2021. 彝语他留话四音格词的韵律和语义特征. 民族语文 2021(6).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Fullest description of Taliu (talu1238), the closest documented Taloid sister of Naruo; would supply the cluster's prosodic profile if Naruo itself stays undescribed (different glottocode, so only a proxy).

sources.citation: 云南省民族识别研究组 [Yunnan Sheng Minzu Shibie Yanjiuzu]. 1954/1955. 永胜水田、倮倮、支里、子彝、崀峨、他鲁等民族的语言, in 云南民族识别参考资料, p. 22 ff. (Glottolog ref 300239).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Earliest primary record of the na21 zu21 (Naruo) language of Yongsheng; a short survey sketch that may include remarks on syllable/tone/prominence.

sources.citation: 朱文旭, 张静 [Zhu Wenxu & Zhang Jing]. 2005. 彝语水田话概况 [Overview of Shuitian Yi]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 2005(4): 67-80. (Glottolog's only descriptive ref attached to nalu1239.)

sources.note: NCPSSD abstract shows it describes the Shuitian (mu33hi44su33 'Muhisu') Yi of Xichang/Xide/Mianning in Liangshan, Sichuan, a Northern Yi lect, NOT Yongsheng Naruo; irrelevant to nalu1239 (Glottolog hh note agrees). Full text login-gated, not downloaded.

sources.note: No Chinese-language article on Naruo found. 他留话 hits (Zhou Decai 2002 他留话概况, 2005; Hu Suhua & Duan Qiuhong 2021 彝语他留话四音格词的韵律和语义特征) concern Taliu = talu1238, a sister Taloid language, not Naruo.
